subject: ventures/ad-slot-sell-through-planner
professional: a newsletter/podcast sponsorship sales or ad-ops manager who plans flat-fee slot inventory each issue (IAB usage: sell-through = sold units / available units; revenue left on the table = unsold units x rate card), paces bookings against a pickup curve and moves the rate card; first checks: sell-through and unsold-value arithmetic, whether the price advice agrees with how full the inventory is, and the pacing projection

evidence.correctness: Ran calc.mjs on the page's own example and on synthetic histories (`node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/f59c5cce-fbdc-5341-97d2-6a5629e767ca/scratchpad/adslot/run.mjs`, `node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/f59c5cce-fbdc-5341-97d2-6a5629e767ca/scratchpad/adslot/r2.mjs`, `node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/f59c5cce-fbdc-5341-97d2-6a5629e767ca/scratchpad/adslot/r3.mjs`) and recomputed by hand from the stated formulas: example sell-through 18/27 = 66.7%, booked $7,300 of $11,550 capacity ($4,250 unsold), recent-4 5/12 = 0.4167 vs prior-4 10/12 = 0.8333; OLS log-log slope with two price levels = (mean ln-rate at 550 - mean at 450)/(ln550-ln450) = (-1.0986+0.6827)/0.2007 = -2.0725 (tool -2.0725); +10% scenario 0.41667*1.1^-2.0725 = 0.3420, $507.84/run (tool identical); pacing at 5 days out interpolates 0.8->0.92 to 0.86, projects 2/0.86 = 2.33 of 4, expected-now 0.8*4*0.86 = 2.752, so 'behind' (tool identical); sold-out anchor 1.15*(f)^-1.2 = 1 at f = 1.1235, grid gives 113 (tool 113). Every number recomputes; the defect is in what the numbers are used to say (domain).
evidence.completeness: Every feature the README and page list runs end to end in calc.mjs and is wired in index.html: summarize/trend, fitElasticity with censoring and fallback, priceScenarios, recommend (+/-25% cap), pacing, lastMinute, packages, diagnose, opt-out. Gaps: the page says 'Replace [the booking curve] with your own history' but there is no input for it (pacing() accepts a curve; index.html never passes one); an unspaced comma CSV with a 3-digit price ('Mar 3,3,2,400') is rejected because the thousands-separator lookahead eats ',400'. Tab-pasted spreadsheet rows and the spaced placeholder format work.
evidence.verification: `node --test` in the subject root: 28 tests, 28 pass (calc, page, usage). Four seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: pacing tolerance 0.5->1.5 SURVIVED, diagnose 'close to sold out' threshold 0.9->0.97 SURVIVED, sold-out excess demand 1.15->1.05 SURVIVED, censoring filter < -> <= CAUGHT. 3 of 4 survived: the thresholds that drive the advice a user acts on are not pinned.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (188 lines, pure functions, no deps), index.html inline module, usage.mjs, all three test files. Clean, small, escapes labels before innerHTML, guards localStorage. Defects: parseHistory's comma regex (calc.mjs:38) is a heuristic that misreads standard unquoted CSV with 3-digit fields and reports the wrong error ('need label, slots offered...'); a European '1.200,50' price silently becomes 1.2; recommend's grid accumulates f += 0.01 in floating point (harmless here). Footer typo 'an qualified advisor' (index.html:120).
evidence.claims: Checked: 'Entirely client-side; nothing is uploaded' (backed: page.test.mjs network test, no fetch in code); 'never moves more than 25%' (backed, calc.mjs:122); sold-out and empty runs left out of the fit (backed, calc.mjs:79); '15% excess demand' labelled (backed, calc.mjs:7); disclaimer and no-warranty footer present; usage events plan_run/example_loaded local-only with DNT/GPC honoured (backed, usage.mjs). Not backed: 'Replace it [booking curve] with your own history' (no UI); FAQ 'sell-through above about 90% usually means you are underpriced' is contradicted by the tool's own recommendation, which tells a 97%-sold seller to lower price. llms.txt source links github.io but served-copy.mjs shows the deployed llms.txt points at marisstella.app (source-only, not a defect).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job as the sales manager: paste 10 runs at $400, 29/30 sold, recent 11/12. The page says 'You are close to sold out ... test a higher price' and, on the same screen, 'Model says lower the price: About $372 per slot'. With the assumed elasticity -1.2 (< -1) any recent run that is not 100% full is told to cut price to the sell-out point, so the headline recommendation is an artifact of the default constant, not the data. Sell-through, unsold value, pacing and package math are usable; the raise/hold/lower call, which the README sells as the main outcome, cannot be relied on without a fitted response.
evidence.domain: Compared against revenue-management practice for fixed perishable inventory: a constant-elasticity curve has no interior optimum (revenue per run is monotone in price for e != -1), so recommend() always lands on either the sell-out price (e < -1) or the +25% cap (e > -1); a practitioner would not let an assumed elasticity pick the direction. The fit pools runs across time without controlling for the falling trend it diagnoses (example: price rises coincide with the decline, fitted e = -2.07 from two price levels, no uncertainty shown) while the trend finding itself says 'check lead time before touching price'. Multiplicative pickup pacing and the IAB-style sell-through/unsold-value definitions are standard and correct. No CPM view, slot position (pre/mid-roll, primary/secondary), or make-goods, all disclosed.

defects.what: With the assumed elasticity -1.2 (< -1) recommend() tells any seller whose recent runs are not 100% full to cut price to the sell-out point; a 97%-sold, flat-price history gets 'You are close to sold out ... test a higher price' and 'Model says lower the price: About $372' on the same screen. The direction is an artifact of the default constant, not the data.

Constant-elasticity revenue has no interior optimum, so recommend() always returns the sell-out price or the +25% cap; the fit pools runs across time without separating price from the falling trend it reports, and shows no uncertainty for a slope from two price levels.

Unquoted comma CSV with a 3-digit field ('Mar 3,3,2,400', the usual spreadsheet export) is rejected: the thousands-separator lookahead treats ',400' as part of the previous number, and the error blames missing columns.
Page tells the user to replace the booking curve with their own history, but there is no input; pacing() is always called with the default curve.
Tests leave the advice thresholds unpinned: pacing tolerance, the 90% 'close to sold out' finding and the 1.15 sold-out excess demand can all change with every test green (3 of 4 mutants survived).
Footer typo 'does not replace an qualified advisor'.

verdict: Small, clean, honest-in-intent tool whose arithmetic is right: six outputs (sell-through, unsold value, trend, fitted slope, a price scenario, pacing) recompute exactly by hand. It misses the bar on claims and verification, and on domain: the raise/hold/lower call the README sells as the main outcome is driven by the assumed elasticity being below -1, so a 97%-sold seller is told on one screen both to test a higher price and to lower it to $372 (run the r3.mjs command in checks). Three of four seeded mutants in the advice thresholds survived, the page promises a custom booking curve it has no input for, and plain comma CSV with 3-digit prices is rejected. Sell-through, unsold-revenue and pacing views are usable today; the price recommendation should be suppressed on an assumed response.
